newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes ease as traders assess July.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes ease as traders assess July.

text.p: Crude oil prices on the U.S. West Coast eased Friday, with business quiet as traders assessed their supply needs for July.
ARCO sold 2,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of Line 63 blended crude to Paramount Refinery. The parcel was priced at $3.50 under July WTI, traders said.

Regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude has been declining steadily relative to U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) for nearly three months after peaking in early March at an 80 cent discount to WTI.
Last Friday BP America sold a cargo to Texaco Transport and Trading at a discount of $1.75, and offered it this week at minus $1.60.
Buyers expected the next cargo to sell at $1.90-$2.00 off July WTI.
Outright prices for ANS ranged $19.15/19.35 a barrel Friday, tracking lower spot and futures markets.
Crude prices, already pressured by South American grades, could come under more pressure if Canadian imports increased by mid-summer as anticipated, traders said.
Heavier valley crudes were seeing flat or easier differentials to posted prices, which were lowered on Tuesday by between 25 and 50 cents, traders said.
